pr_title: obj: Avoid empty names and meshes
pr_body:
This PR updates the obj importer to properly name imported meshes and permits it to skip meshes that do not contain geometry. This fixes at least one crash (#70539) and several warnings and avoids unnecessary meshes being generated when importing obj files that do not contain geometry that is not assigned to a named object (such as when exporting from Blender).

Fixes #70539
pr_comments: I wonder if empty meshes might have a wanted usecase in cases where a different pivot might be wanted. I recall this being a pretty common approach.
There seems to be disagreement so I can't propose a merge.

@fire tbf I'm leaning more towards a merge. My doubt was regarding the use of void objects as pivots, but the OBJ format doesn't allow defining the transform of an object, making that usecase useless per se.

Unless @realkotob (who reacted to my doubt with favourable reactions) doesn't have a particular usecase (please answer), I'd just merge and see if anybody who has a useful way of using empty untranslated objects complains.

@fire I don't see disagreement at the moment, so I'm unsure what could move this forward. (Other than rebasing, but I will only do that if there is a chance for the PR to get merged.)

The reason why I propose to generally ignore empty meshes is that `ImporterMesh` considers it an error to have empty meshes (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blame/master/scene/resources/importer_mesh.cpp#L677, you wrote that check yourself), so I would expect them to cause issues down the road. This commit thus fixes that error for most obj files generated from tools like Blender. If there should be any use case for empty objects in obj files, I would assume that a separate patch is needed to import them as non-mesh nodes. Any use case we support should not spam the console with error messages (imho).

That said, I can also split this into two PRs (default name here, empty objects in a new PR) and make the second PR only skip the creation of empty objects that clearly are not intended to be there. That would fix the issues I see in my projects, while preserving the current behaviour (including error messages and potential issues down the road) whenever the user intentionally adds empty objects.

I would appreciate if you, or any other Godot core developer with suitable authority, could decide which path we take so I can update the PR(s) accordingly.
FBX pivot baking enhancement is being tracked here https://github.com/godotengine/FBX2glTF/issues/25

issue_context.title: OBJ files imported as Scene crashes when selecting the mesh in import settings.
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 Beta10

### System information

Ubuntu 22.04 (Tuxedo OS)

### Issue description

After importing an *.obj file as a scene, if you click on the mesh in the import settings Godot crashes.

![Screenshot from 2022-12-24 14-38-23](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25522325/209452619-3c0ed61b-deaa-4fb6-8ff5-5aa11ff4ed33.png)

I the above screenshot, clicking in the circled area will crash Godot.

### Steps to reproduce

Import .obj file into a project.
Select the file.
Go to import setting.
Change OBJ As Mesh to Scene.
Click Reimport.
Click Save Scenes, Re-Import, and Restart.
Once restarted, open the advanced import settings on the object.
Click the are circled in the description, or in the meshes tab.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A

Specifically, I lack the distribution rights of the .obj files I am using.  Any .obj file should do, this happened to me on at least 4 different .obj files.

review_comments: I would use the class name of the mesh.

The default name will be used for multiple classes throughout the import process (`ArrayMesh`, `ImporterMesh` and `ImporterMeshInstance3D`), so I'm not sure if adding significant complexity to use the name of each individual class if no name is set is a good idea.
